brief: A PLA cup: 60 mm outside diameter and 80 mm tall, with 2 mm walls and a 3 mm floor, open at the top. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

intent.summary: A simple open-top cylindrical cup intended to be 3D printed in PLA, defined by outer diameter, height, wall thickness and floor thickness.
stated: User states it carries no load, so there is no load case
implied: Being a 'cup' with an open top implies it is meant to hold something (liquid, granular material, or small objects), even though the user explicitly disclaims structural load
PLA material implies fused deposition modeling (FDM) manufacture is likely intended, since PLA is a common desktop 3D-printing filament
A floor thickness distinct from wall thickness implies the cup has a flat circular base closing the bottom
60 mm outside diameter with 2 mm walls implies an inside diameter on the order of 56 mm, though exact inner geometry depends on whether walls taper or are constant
unstated: Whether the cup needs to hold liquid (requiring watertightness) or is purely decorative/dry-use
Any thermal exposure (hot liquids) which matters because PLA has a low heat-deflection temperature
Surface finish or printing orientation requirements
Whether the top rim needs a lip, chamfer, or specific edge treatment
Whether the base needs feet, a foot ring, or anti-slip feature for stability
Any requirement for stacking with other cups
Food-safety requirements if intended to contact food or drink
Color, print infill percentage, or layer orientation affecting strength even though 'no load case' is claimed
Whether the cup must be dishwasher- or microwave-safe
out_of_scope: Load-bearing analysis, since the brief explicitly excludes a load case
Print process parameters (nozzle temp, layer height, infill)
risk_signals: None indicating physical danger from structural failure, since the user explicitly states no load case

Potential unstated risk: if intended for hot beverages, PLA's low heat tolerance could cause deformation and burns or spills, but the brief does not mention hot liquid use so this is only a latent concern
Potential unstated risk: if used for food/drink, food-safety of the PLA filament and print process is not addressed

assumptions.statement: The cup is a round, single-cavity cylindrical container with constant 2 mm wall thickness from floor to rim.
assumptions.rationale: Brief describes outside diameter and wall thickness without specifying taper or cross-section shape; cylindrical is the conventional reading of 'cup'.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: If the cup is meant to taper or be non-circular, the declared diameter and roundness no longer describe the part correctly.

assumptions.statement: The cup's top is a plain open rim with no lip, chamfer, handle or lid feature.
assumptions.rationale: Brief only specifies 'open at the top' with no additional rim feature described.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: A missing lip or handle feature would not match user expectations for handling or pouring, though the core geometry (diameter, height, walls, floor) still holds.

assumptions.statement: The cup is used at ambient temperature, not for hot liquids, and no food-contact or watertightness certification is required beyond ordinary FDM print quality.
assumptions.rationale: Brief gives no load case and no mention of contents; PLA has low heat-deflection temperature and FDM prints are not inherently watertight, so a 'cup' purpose is assumed to be light, ambient, non-critical use (e.g. holding small dry items or cool liquids briefly).
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: If intended for hot beverages, the PLA walls could soften or deform, risking spills or burns; if intended to hold liquid long-term, untreated FDM layer lines may leak.

document.name: Open-top cylindrical cup
document.description: A round PLA cup: a solid outer cylinder with a cylindrical cavity subtracted from the floor thickness up through the open top.

parameters.description: Thickness of the cylindrical side wall
Thickness of the solid base closing the bottom
Diameter of the interior cavity, derived from the outer diameter and wall thickness
Height of the cavity cutter, starting above the floor and overshooting the top so the cut runs cleanly out through the open top

features.description: Solid outer cylinder of the cup, floor to rim
Cavity cutter, starting just above the floor and running past the rim so the top stays open
The outer cylinder less the cavity, leaving a floor and side wall with an open top

answer.rationale: The cup is two concentric cylinders: a solid outer_body of outer_diameter x height, and a cavity cylinder of inner_diameter (= outer_diameter - 2*wall_thickness) sitting on top of the floor_thickness, overshooting the rim by 1 mm so the subtraction cleanly opens the top. A single subtract leaves the terminal solid: a floor of floor_thickness, a wall of wall_thickness, and an open top, all driven parametrically from outer_diameter, height, wall_thickness and floor_thickness so changing any one keeps the others consistent.
